extractions.value: Postmortem examination revealed vacuolation of motor neurons in caudal spinal cord (T12 to sacral), with sparing of motor neurons superior to this. Electron microscopy showed membrane-lined vacuoles with invaginations containing cytoplasmic matter, suggestive of hyperswollen lysosomes. No significant lymphocytic infiltrate was found, likely due to extended immunosuppressive treatment. CD68 revealed microglial reaction in gray matter; GFAP demonstrated marked gray matter gliosis. Dorsal root ganglion showed neuronal loss with macrophage infiltration and attack of ganglion cells. One residual ganglion cell contained a round, hyaline inclusion similar in appearance to a Lewy body, not observed on immunohistochemistry for p62 or alpha synuclein. This is the second report in the literature to demonstrate vacuolation of spinal cord motor neurons in a patient with SPS and the first to provide EM examination findings of the spinal cord.
extractions.quote: Microscopic examination of the spinal cord revealed vacuolation of motor neurons in the caudal segments (T12 to sacral; Fig. 1a), with sparing of motor neurons superior to this. Electron microscopy revealed these vacuoles to be lined by a membrane and contain invaginations that contained cytoplasmic matter (Fig. 1b–d). These then appeared to ''bud off'' from the inner surface of the vacuole into the vacuole itself and degenerate. A number of lipofuscin-containing lysosomes with features of hydropic swelling were observed in the cytoplasm of affected cells, suggesting that the vacuoles may represent hyperswollen lysosomes. There was no significant lymphocytic infiltrate, as has been described in other case reports/series,3,4 likely because of extended immunosuppressive treatment. Immunohistochemistry: CD68 revealed a microglial reaction in the gray matter; GFAP demonstrated marked gray matter gliosis. There was no associated lymphocytic or neutrophil reaction and no apparent long-tract degeneration. Histology of the dorsal root ganglion revealed neuronal loss with macrophage infiltration and attack of ganglion cells (Fig. 1e). One residual ganglion cell contained a round, hyaline inclusion, similar in appearance to a Lewy body (Fig. 1f). These structures were not observed on immunohistochemistry for p62 or alpha synuclein.
